newsitem.title: USA: CompUSA sees same-store sales up 5-6 pct in Q2.
newsitem.headline: CompUSA sees same-store sales up 5-6 pct in Q2.

text.p: CompUSA Inc Chief Executive Officer Jim Halpin said he expects the retailer's same-store sales to grow between five and six percent in the second quarter, which covers the key Christmas holiday season.
Halpin told Reuters in a telephone interview that retail sales of laptops "are on fire" but acknowledged that sales of desktop computers "are a litle slow".

He refused to comment on a Salomon Brothers research report that said the growth of retail computer sales has in recent weeks slowed to zero from three-to-four percent in the first quarter which ended September 28.
Halpin said October is always a lackluster month and that Christmas sales would be key in determining how well its business does.
"We are cautiously optimistic about the holiday season," he said.
CompUSA's stock fell 5-1/2 on Tuesday and was down another 4-5/8 at 46-7/8 on on the New York Stock Exchange at noon Wednesday.
Halpin refused to comment on the stock price decline but said CompUSA's business remains strong. "We are all very happy with our business," he said.
CompUSA earlier reported first quarter net profit of $14.5 million, or $0.31 per share, up from $6.2 million, or $0.15 per share, in the same period last year.
Same-store sales were up 7.2 percent and total sales rose 26.7 percent to $991 million.
Halpin said the slowdown in retail sales was compensated for by continuing strong performances in the company's direct sales to corporations and its services business.
In the second quarter of fiscal 1996, which ended last December 23, CompUSA saw same-store sales grow 10.5 percent.
The current second quarter ends on December 28.
